_readme: DRAFT candidates. Every entry has verified=false. Open each PDF, confirm the answer and page (page numbers for the two slide decks were counted from slide order; the Kohli report uses its printed page footers), then set verified=true. run_eval must ignore verified=false. Answers must match WHAT THE DOCUMENT SAYS, not real-world truth: never 'correct' an expected_answer from memory or the web. expected_answer 'REFUSAL' means the exact refusal string is correct. relevant = any listed (doc,page) counts as a retrieval hit. types: text | table | chart | multi | image | unanswerable.

questions.question: How does GraphRAG differ from traditional RAG?
questions.expected_answer: Traditional RAG relies only on text similarity to find separate chunks; GraphRAG organizes information into nodes (entities) and edges (relationships) so the AI can follow connections across data points to answer multi-step questions.

questions.question: What is Neo4j?
questions.expected_answer: A native graph database designed to store, manage and query highly connected data using nodes, relationships and properties.

questions.question: What does the Cypher MATCH clause do?
questions.expected_answer: It finds a graph pattern, for example MATCH (m:Movie) RETURN m.

questions.question: Which nodes are extracted from the Inception chunk in Step 2?
questions.expected_answer: Movie Inception (released 2010), Person Christopher Nolan, Person Leonardo DiCaprio, Genre Sci-Fi.

questions.question: Why should documents be chunked before graph extraction?
questions.expected_answer: Smaller context, easier extraction, and better retrieval later.

questions.question: What are the four steps of the query/answer phase of the complete GraphRAG pipeline?
questions.expected_answer: Question, Text to Cypher (LLM generates query), Graph retrieval (Neo4j traverses links), Answer (LLM uses graph context).

questions.question: What are the components of the Simple RAG flow shown in the diagram?
questions.expected_answer: Structured and unstructured data become chunks, which are embedded into a vector DB (text embedding model), retrieved as chunks, then an LLM does response generation.

questions.question: What are the core components of an AI agent?
questions.expected_answer: Reasoning (core LLM engine), Planning, Memory, Perception (input layer), Action (execution layer).

questions.question: What are the four types of agent memory?
questions.expected_answer: Short-term, long-term, working and episodic memory.

questions.question: What example is given for a reactive agent?
questions.expected_answer: A thermostat that turns on the AC the moment it hits 25 degrees C.

questions.question: Which agentic framework is best for role-based collaboration between specialised agents?
What are the five layers of the guardrail architecture?
questions.expected_answer: Input rails, dialog rails, retrieval rails, execution rails (kill-switch), output rails.

questions.question: What are the five cost optimization techniques for cutting an $8,000/month agent bill?
questions.expected_answer: Model tiering, semantic caching, optimize workflows, batch processing, monitor and limit.

questions.question: What is Denial of Wallet?
questions.expected_answer: Infinite loops causing uncontrolled API calls and high financial cost.

questions.question: What are the five steps of the error handling workflow for autonomous agents?
questions.expected_answer: Validation, detection, action formulation, logging, human-in-the-loop.

questions.question: What three things does RAG enable an AI agent to do?
questions.expected_answer: Access external or private data, reduce dependence on static training knowledge, generate responses grounded in real information.
questions.note: Distractor test: the GraphRAG deck also discusses RAG. Correct page is the agentic deck.
